screen35-a1.glyph: two horizontal lines, the lower one shorter
screen35-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Menu" - read only to know what to watch for when testing; not used in the verdict
screen35-a1.convention_relied_on: two/three stacked lines = open the main menu (hamburger) - my reading; the two-line variant is slightly less canonical than three lines
screen35-a1.initial_rationale: no label, but two stacked horizontal lines is a recognizable variant of the hamburger menu convention - common-icon exemption pending the behavioural test
screen35-a1.deciding_evidence: tapping it slid a navigation drawer in from the left, exactly what the menu convention promises; the missing label is not a barrier; tested once on screen1-a1 and carried to this identical control

screen35-a2.description: pill in the header with a sparkle glyph and the words 'Get Plus'

screen35-a2.initial_rationale: visible words 'Get Plus' with a sparkle; 'Plus' is a product name a first-time user has no way to decode, and nothing says it costs money
screen35-a2.deciding_evidence: tapping opened a paywall ('ChatGPT Plus', 'Upgrade for $19.99', 'Renews monthly') - a paid monthly subscription the words 'Get Plus' never mentioned; tested once on screen1-a2 and carried to this identical control
screen35-a2.recommendation: say what it is and that it is paid, e.g. 'Upgrade to Plus (paid plan)'
